title: What Is Democracy?
summary: Voting, rights, rules and why many countries choose their leaders.

steps.title: Rule by the people
sentences: In a democracy, people choose their leaders by voting.
The word comes from Greek: demos means people and kratos means rule.
India is the world's largest democracy by number of voters.

steps.title: Rights and duties
sentences: Citizens have rights, such as freedom of speech and equality before the law.
They also have duties, such as obeying laws and protecting public property.

steps.title: How voting works
sentences: In India, citizens aged 18 and above can vote.
Elections are run by the Election Commission of India, and Electronic Voting Machines record votes.
The vote is secret, so no one can force you to choose.

steps.title: Why it matters
sentences: A democracy lets people change leaders peacefully and speak about problems.
Free news, courts and citizens who ask questions help keep it healthy.
Learning to listen to different views is the first step of democracy.

facts: Athens in ancient Greece had an early form of democracy, but only some people could vote.
India held its first general election in 1951-52.
The voting age in India was lowered from 21 to 18 in 1989.

quiz.q: At what age can Indian citizens vote?
What does the word democracy come from?
quiz.why: It comes from Greek words meaning people and rule.

notes: Neutral civics explanation; no party or leader is discussed.
